PullRequest.Title: chat: expose sandbox credential masking in settings
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #346422

### Summary

- Add `chat.agent.sandbox.credentials.envVars` with the title **Masked environment variables**, ordered after Git and GitHub CLI authentication in the sandbox Credentials group.
- Describe the environment-variable map and required `injectHosts` arrays in the VS Code and Agent Host schemas. Provide JSON completion templates for the setting, variable entries, and host arrays.
- Forward defined maps to local and remote hosts through ordinary sandbox configuration, without managed-policy presentation/resolution or a machine-only scope.
- Cover schema validation, grouping/order, forwarding, and live runtime updates after create/resume.

The default remains `null` (omit the credential override); an explicit empty object forwards an empty map. Only variable names and destination hosts are configured, not secret values. The runtime remains responsible for destination-pattern validation.

### How to test

1. Open Settings and search for `@id:chat.agent.sandbox.credentials.envVars`. Confirm its title and placement alongside the sandbox credential authentication settings.
2. In Settings JSON, use Ctrl+Space to insert an environment-variable entry and its `injectHosts` array:

   ```json
   "chat.agent.sandbox.credentials.envVars": {
     "API_TOKEN": { "injectHosts": ["api.example.com"] }
   }
   ```

3. With the Copilot Agent Host sandbox enabled, change the map and verify it is forwarded as `sandbox.credentials.envVars`. Set it to `{}` to forward an empty map.

### Validation

- `pnpm run compile-client` — passed, zero compilation errors.
- The following focused Electron test command — passed, 65 tests:

  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\sandboxConfigForSdk.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\preferences\test\browser\settingsTreeModels.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\common\terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\common\sandboxSettingsReader.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\terminalContrib\chatAgentTools\test\browser\agentHostSandboxForwarder.test.ts --grep "credential|sandbox search keywords|sandboxSettingsReader|AgentHostSandboxForwarder" --reporter dot
  ```

- `pnpm run eslint src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/sandboxConfigSchema.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sandboxConfigForSdk.test.ts src/vs/platform/sandbox/common/settings.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/browser/settingsTreeModels.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/test/browser/settingsTreeModels.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/common/sandboxSettingsReader.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/common/terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/agentHostSandboxForwarder.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/common/terminalChatAgentToolsConfiguration.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed before commit.
- Direct JSON language-service probes against the compiled schema — passed all five completion positions, snippet expansion, and valid/invalid shape checks.
- Live credential injection against external services and full integration/smoke suites were not run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Settings or edit JSON for masked environment-variable credentials
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Schema registration and settings-tree label formatting are local synchronous metadata work; JSON validation/completion walks the configured environment-variable entries before the edit is accepted. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is on this UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configured variable names and injectHosts strings; normal configurations are expected to contain a small credential map.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single settings UI/configuration validation path; no parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The registered schema and display metadata are static. There is no new runtime cache or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the schema performs local collection-proportional validation and introduces no expensive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large hand-authored maps would increase schema-validation CPU linearly, but the diff adds only the validation required for the new structured setting and provides no evidence of realistically large cardinality or user-visible latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: local validation and completion metadata are required by the setting and bounded by a realistically small user-authored map.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect a local or remote Agent Host and forward the initial sandbox configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After a host advertises the sandbox schema, the forwarder reads the effective settings once, compares the complete sandbox object, and dispatches one RootConfigChanged action to each connection whose state differs. Host-side handling persists root configuration and notifies configuration consumers; session-specific SDK updates occur only for eligible active sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch RootConfigChanged containing the sandbox configuration, including credentials.envVars
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one initial dispatch per connected local or remote host that advertises the schema and has differing state; the credential map is grouped into that single dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-dispatch-per-connection boundary already forwarded the complete sandbox object; the diff only adds the optional credential map to that grouped object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the newly connected host has the workbench sandbox policy; dispatch itself is asynchronous/optimistic from the workbench perspective.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and atomically write the complete persisted root configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued write per accepted RootConfigChanged action on each receiving host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every RootConfigChanged action already persisted root configuration through the same queued write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued and not awaited by client dispatch; off the workbench connection critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply effective sandbox configuration through the Copilot SDK session options update
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one update for each eligible active Copilot session whose serialized effective sandbox config differs; inactive sessions are skipped and each session is serialized by its config sequencer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing sandbox root-config changes already used this per-active-session SDK update path; the diff adds credential data to the effective config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in background configuration synchronization and is not required for the workbench connection to complete, though it must finish before that live session uses the updated credential policy.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Connected Agent Hosts, active Copilot sessions on each host, and credential-map size. The effective host cardinality is one grouped dispatch per connection, not one dispatch per environment variable.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection dispatches are iterated synchronously. Eligible sessions react independently, while each session's SDK updates are serialized by _configSequencer; aggregate concurrency can reach the number of active sessions, as it already does for sandbox changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The workbench caches the desired sandbox object in _desired across connections and invalidates it only on relevant setting changes. Each session compares JSON against _appliedConfig and skips an unchanged SDK update; inactive sessions apply current configuration when activated/resumed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the grouped per-connection dispatch, queued filesystem persistence, active-session filter, and per-session serialization based on the traced callers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may have multiple remote connections or active sessions, but typical credential maps and simultaneously active sessions are small; no evidence indicates a new large fan-out or high-frequency trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff extends an existing grouped configuration boundary, does not create per-entry calls, and preserves equality checks, inactive-session filtering, and per-session sequencing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live-edit or reset chat.agent.sandbox.credentials.envVars while Agent Hosts and sessions are running
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A configuration event invalidates the cached desired object, computes it once, and pushes changed sandbox state to each connected host. Each receiving host persists root state and active sessions serialize and apply a changed SDK sandbox configuration. Intermediate edits are not explicitly coalesced at the workbench, but configuration events occur on accepted setting updates and per-session work is sequenced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one grouped RootConfigChanged action with the updated environment-variable map
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per connected host whose current sandbox value differs, regardless of the number of map entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changes to this newly exposed setting did not previously trigger forwarding; other sandbox settings already followed this exact grouped path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for live policy propagation; calls are issued immediately after the accepted configuration update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the resulting root configuration via temporary-file write and rename
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued atomic persistence operation per accepted host update; repeated accepted edits queue in order.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The persistence boundary existed for every RootConfigChanged action; the new setting can now trigger it when the user changes that setting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by the workbench dispatch, but consumes host filesystem I/O in the background.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call the Copilot SDK to apply the updated effective sandbox config
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per eligible active session when credentials alter the serialized effective config; no call for inactive sessions or unchanged serialized configs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This credential setting could not previously alter running sessions, while other sandbox settings already triggered the same update mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for each running session to begin enforcing the new credential policy; per-session calls are sequenced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Accepted edits times connected hosts and eligible active sessions, with serialization bytes proportional to the complete credential map. Effective cardinality is per host/session, not per variable or host pattern.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-host dispatches are immediate; active sessions can update concurrently in aggregate, while each individual session queues updates on its sequencer. Filesystem writes are serialized by _rootConfigWrite.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The desired workbench object is recomputed once per accepted relevant setting event and reused across connections. Deep equality avoids dispatch when host state already matches. Session-level serialized-config comparison suppresses redundant SDK calls; there is no explicit cross-event latest-value coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed event reachability, boundary counts, and sequencing; lower confidence that realistic editing frequency or cardinality would produce measurable degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rapid auto-saved JSON edits could create multiple accepted updates, but this is an infrequent user configuration workflow, maps are expected to be small, writes are serialized, and no evidence establishes a harmful burst at realistic session counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: live propagation is the feature's required behavior, each map is grouped rather than fanned out per entry, unchanged/inactive work is filtered, and realistic update frequency does not establish excessive IPC or I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the next terminal-sandboxed command after changing the credential setting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Because the credential key was added to the shared sandbox-setting list, TerminalSandboxEngine marks its generated config stale even though that engine does not read credentials.envVars. The next wrapped command regenerates the sandbox JSON config before command execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Regenerate and write the terminal sandbox configuration file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one deferred rewrite after one or many credential-setting changes before the next command; the boolean invalidation coalesces repeated changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changing this credential setting did not previously invalidate the terminal sandbox config because the key was absent from SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The single rewrite is on the next sandboxed command's wrapping critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Credential-setting changes between terminal commands; repeated changes before a command collapse to one rewrite and do not scale with credential-map entries in the terminal engine.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single engine invalidation and one awaited config regeneration on the next wrapping operation; no per-entry or per-session fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The engine's _needsForceUpdateConfigFile boolean coalesces all invalidations until the next generated config, then resets.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the unrelated key causes one deferred rewrite; high confidence that repeated edits coalesce to one rewrite before command use.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact config-file write duration varies by filesystem, but this is one small deferred local write after an infrequent settings change and is commonly subsumed by command-specific config refreshes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: although the invalidation is broader than necessary, it creates only one coalesced small local rewrite after an infrequent configuration edit, insufficient for a concrete user-visible performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and traced settings UI, initial forwarding, live updates, host persistence, active-session SDK synchronization, and terminal config invalidation. The change adds no per-entry boundary fan-out or unbounded retention; expensive work is grouped per connection/session, filtered for unchanged or inactive state, and sequenced. No issue met the high-confidence performance-reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
